record.paper_title: On some open problems in Diophantine approximation
record.original_question: Let Lambda be a full-rank lattice in R^(n+1). Define its homogeneous minimum N(Lambda) as the infimum of |z_0 z_1 ... z_n| over all nonzero z = (z_0, z_1, ..., z_n) in Lambda. Call a lattice algebraic when it is obtained from the embeddings of a basis 1, theta_1, ..., theta_n of a totally real algebraic field of degree n+1, followed by multiplication by a diagonal matrix with nonzero diagonal entries. For n >= 2, must every lattice Lambda with N(Lambda) > 0 be algebraic?

evidence.quote: Suppose that 1, θ1 , ..., θn form a basis of a totally real algebraic field K = Q(θ) of degree n + 1.
Let G be a diagonal matrix of dimension (n+1)×(n+1) with non-zero diagonal elements. We consider a lattice of the form Λ = G Ω Zn+1 . Lattices of such a type are known as algebraic lattices.
For an arbitrary lattice Λ ⊂ Rn+1 we consider its homogeneous minima N (Λ) = inf |z0 z1 · · · zn |.
A famous Oppenheim conjecture supposes that in the case n ⩾ 2 any lattice Λ satisfying N (L) > 0 is an algebraic lattice. This conjecture is still open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer n ≥ 2, let Λ ⊂ ℝ^(n+1) be a full-rank lattice. Define its homogeneous minimum by
   N(Λ) = inf { |z_0 z_1 ⋯ z_n| : z = (z_0, z_1, …, z_n) ∈ Λ, z ≠ 0 }.

Call Λ an algebraic lattice if there exist a totally real algebraic number field K of degree n+1 over ℚ, with elements 1, θ_1, …, θ_n forming a ℚ-basis of K, and (real) embeddings σ_0, σ_1, …, σ_n : K → ℝ such that, setting
   Ω = ( σ_i(θ_j) )_{0 ≤ i,j ≤ n}   (with θ_0 := 1),
one has Λ = G · Ω · ℤ^(n+1), where G is a diagonal (n+1)×(n+1) matrix with nonzero real diagonal entries.

Question: Is it true that every full-rank lattice Λ ⊂ ℝ^(n+1) with N(Λ) > 0 must be an algebraic lattice?
artifact.category_tag: Oppenheim conjecture on product of linear forms / algebraic lattices
artifact.status_search_result: This is the classical Oppenheim conjecture on products of linear forms (the lattice/algebraic-form version, distinct from the quadratic-form Oppenheim conjecture proved by Margulis). It is closely related to the Littlewood conjecture and is widely regarded as still open for every n ≥ 2; only partial results (e.g., Einsiedler–Katok–Lindenstrauss-type measure rigidity, bounds on Hausdorff dimension of exceptions) are known.

status_evidence.title: On some open problems in Diophantine approximation (arXiv:1202.4539)
status_evidence.snippet: A famous Oppenheim conjecture supposes that in the case n ⩾ 2 any lattice Λ satisfying N(Λ) > 0 is an algebraic lattice. This conjecture is still open.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated as still open.

status_evidence.title: Oppenheim conjecture — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Oppenheim's conjectures; the product-of-linear-forms version connected to Littlewood's conjecture remains an outstanding open problem.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the product-of-linear-forms / algebraic lattice version is reported.
